comments.author: Brin
comments.body_html:
I’m not saying “do it”, and I have absolutely no idea how practical it is (probably not at all), but if it’s something you’d actually like to investigate…

CWX’s megamod has an option to replace the reserve alarm (hermetic exfil switch) with a user-supplied audio file.

If that basic code approach would also work for changing the hideout music track (and, I suppose, if CWX is ok with you borrowing the code if that’s the route you go), I wonder if it would be possible to add a “slot” to a hideout zone (e.g. Rest Space) that can accept the records (one at a time, obviously), and then have each different in-game record call on a pre-defined filename (e.g. track_1, track_2, etc.) in the client mod’s file tree.

Then you just put “dummy” tracks in the distributed mod and let people replace them with whatever they want.

It’s probably much more work than is worth doing though.

ETA: The cultist circle might also be a useful example to look at, particularly the slot it has for the sacred amulet.

comments.author: NorvinskSila
comments.body_html:
I see you’re already adding Atlantic Records stuff. How about Laura Branigan’s LPs or even singles? For an easter egg: unreleased “Branigan (1981)” - just a blank white envelope with hand-filled info; blank white label, again, filled in by hand. Then lots of released albums from “Branigan” 1982 to “Over My Heart” with a typical Atlantic Records label as a common stuff… Though they were rather rare in Russia, ‘cause Laura’s music was not officially sold in USSR.
Though I don’t completely understand the purpose of this mode. Despite the fact that I once liked the idea of filling the game with as many useless items as possible, the more mods to add useless items I download, the more difficult it becomes to develop in the game, because they take away loose loot places where you could spawn items for barter, for hideouts and other useful things.
